But lately, I’ll just wake up and the whole morning goes by, and I’ll skip breakfast without even meaning to. And then lunch rolls around, and again, I don't even realize I'm skipping it. And then by the time dinner comes, my wife—she's a really great cook, she puts a lot of effort into our meals—she'll make something nice, and I just sit there and pick at my plate. I can tell it bothers her because she worked hard on it, but I just can't bring myself to actually eat a full meal. And I really started to notice the physical effect of it the other day when I was getting dressed, because my jeans are starting to feel really loose. Like, my regular everyday jeans that usually fit perfectly, they were just sagging, and I actually had to pull my belt a whole notch tighter just to keep them up. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, yeah, actually, sleep has been... it's been really weird lately. I mean, I'm sleeping, technically. It's not like I'm lying awake staring at the ceiling from the moment my head hits the pillow. I usually fall asleep okay, especially since I'm just so drained by the end of the day anyway from doing absolutely nothing. But the problem is, it's just so broken up. It's like I can't get a solid, continuous stretch of rest anymore. 

What happens is, I'll go to bed, say, around eleven or midnight, and I'll be out, but then without fail, I'll wake up around four or five in the morning. And it's not like a gentle waking up where you just roll over and go back to sleep. It's this sudden, wide-awake feeling, and my brain just instantly kicks into gear. And it's never about anything good, either. It's always the stressful stuff. I'll just lie there, staring into the dark, and suddenly I'm thinking about the bills that are due, or how much longer our savings are going to last with me not working, or even just random stuff, like those unfinished music tracks I've got sitting on my computer that I haven't had the energy to touch in weeks. 

It's like my mind decides that 4:30 AM is the perfect time to review every single thing I'm worried about or haven't accomplished. And once that starts, forget it. The sleep is just gone. I might toss and turn for another hour or two, maybe doze off for ten minutes here and there, but it's not real sleep. It's that frustrating, half-awake state where you know you're not resting. So by the time my wife's alarm actually goes off and the sun is coming up, I feel like I've already lived a whole day in my head. I end up feeling completely exhausted and tired before the day even officially starts. It’s just this cycle where I wake up tired, drag myself through the day feeling heavy, and then can't even get a good night's sleep to fix it. So yeah, the sleep is definitely not great right now.

Just this physical heaviness that I can't seem to shake off. It's not just that I don't want to do things, it's like my body is actually lagging behind my brain, or maybe my brain is lagging too, I'm not even sure anymore. 

Like, take getting out of bed, for instance. It used to be, alarm goes off, or I just wake up, and boom, feet on the floor, ready to start the day. Now? I just lie there. It's like the signal from my brain to my muscles gets lost somewhere along the way. I'll lie there for another thirty, forty-five minutes just trying to muster the physical energy to throw the covers off. 

And it's the same with the small stuff during the day. You mentioned taking a shower—that feels like a monumental task. I'll sit on the edge of the bed or on the couch, knowing I need to go wash up, but the thought of standing up, walking to the bathroom, turning on the water, actually washing myself... it just seems exhausting before I even start. I'll just sit there, staring into space. 

Even with things I used to do without thinking. Like, I'll sit down at the kitchen table with my laptop open. I used to hop on there, check job boards, maybe tweak my resume, whatever. Now, I'll literally sit there with the screen glowing in my face for ages, just staring at it, before I even move my hands to type or, like, plug in the keyboard. It's ridiculous. I'll look at the keys and think, "Okay, type," but my hands just rest there on the desk. It’s this weird delay between knowing I should do something and actually initiating the movement to do it. It’s incredibly frustrating because I know I’m not doing anything, I know I’m just sitting there, but I just can't seem to make myself move at a normal speed. Everything is just dragged out and takes ten times the effort it should.

Yeah, actually... it's funny you ask that, because right before this whole low spell started, before I got all heavy and stuck like I was just talking about, I actually had this run where things were the complete opposite.

It’s wild how different that feels compared to now, where I can barely get myself to look at the screen, let alone care about an interruption.
